en: Jupiter is so massive that over 1,300 Earths could fit inside its volume.
The Moon orbits Earth at an average distance of about 384,400 kilometers.
On the Mohs hardness scale, talc ranks as a one while diamond ranks as a ten.
The highest officially recorded air temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley.
About 97 percent of Earth's water is salty ocean water, leaving only three percent as freshwater.
Sunlight takes approximately eight minutes and twenty seconds to travel 150 million kilometers to Earth.
A magnitude 8.0 earthquake releases about 32 times more energy than a magnitude 7.0 earthquake.
It takes nature approximately 500 years to form just one inch of fertile topsoil.
Venus is hotter than Mercury, reaching surface temperatures of about 465 degrees Celsius.
Between 1969 and 1972, exactly twelve astronauts walked on the lunar surface during six Apollo missions.
An average cumulus cloud contains water droplets that collectively weigh about 1.1 million pounds.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo ejected roughly 10 cubic kilometers of magma into the atmosphere.
